bullets.title: NVDA Vera Rubin enters full production; Jensen bullish on AI PCs and job creation
bullets.body: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin agentic AI platform entered full production globally, with Taiwan server makers deploying pod-scale multi-rack systems. Jensen Huang called AI PCs a 'new beginning' on par with the smartphone revolution, and dismissed AI job-loss fears as 'complete nonsense.' NVDA networking business projected to do ~$400B in revenue this year and ~$600B next year, dwarfing PC chip contributions.

bullets.title: NVDA options rotation: sweepers moving from June to July/Sept contracts
bullets.body: Options traders are closing June NVDA positions for profits and rolling capital into July and September expiration contracts, with sweeper activity continuing throughout the session.

bullets.title: Anthropic confidential S-1 filing seen as bullish read-through for AI infrastructure suppliers
bullets.body: Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft S-1 to the SEC for its IPO, with Polymarket pricing a 76% chance it goes public before OpenAI. One trader's gut reaction: 'If Anthropic is filing, the numbers must be strong,' calling it a direct positive for NVDA, MU, SNDK, and LITE as generative AI infrastructure beneficiaries.

bullets.title: MU options premium surpasses SPY+QQQ combined; market cap crosses $1T
bullets.body: Micron's options premium exceeded SPY and QQQ combined at the open—a pattern last seen with NVDA in July 2024. MU market cap surpassed $1 trillion last week, a 10x+ increase over the prior year.

bullets.title: ARM surges from $134 to $413 in 2.5 months; trader flags stretched valuation
bullets.body: ARM ADRs rose 12% at Monday's open and have rallied from $134 to $413 in just 2.5 months (208% gain). One trader noted the move 'feels a tad excessive here' but remains net positive, and regrets not using options for even larger gains.

bullets.title: AAOI surges 20%+ on optical supercycle thesis; bullish conviction building
bullets.body: AAOI rose 20.1% on Monday, with multiple fintwit accounts citing it as the leading US optical long and a potential SNDK-like runner. One trader's Friday call options were up 55-80%. Historical precedent cited: 'Shorting optical companies during supercycles has historically been unprofitable—Citron found this out.'

bullets.title: NBIS up 212% YTD; bulls target $100B market cap from ~$60B
bullets.body: Nebius (NBIS) extended gains +18.2% on the day, up 212.2% YTD. Multiple accounts cited NBIS as the premier neocloud play for agentic AI, with one trader calling it the stock they'd go 'all-in' on. Current market cap ~$60B; one bull sees a path to $100B. CRWV flagged as structurally impaired by high debt, IREN by infinite ATM dilution.

bullets.title: SNOW earnings print cited as spark for software sector surge; IGV +15% in 5 days
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts attributed the software sector's three-day +14% run (best since October 2001) to the SNOW earnings print acting as a positive catalyst. Software ETF IGV rose 15% since last Wednesday's close and was up 3%+ premarket Monday.

bullets.title: MRVL flagged as top S&P 500 addition candidate for June 5; launches 102.4 Tbps switch silicon
bullets.body: Quant models rank MRVL as the #1 addition to S&P 500 on June 5 (announcement expected at 5:15pm EDT post-close). Separately, Marvell introduced Teralynx T100, the industry's first 102.4 Tbps switch silicon purpose-built for AI workloads. VRT also cited as a potential addition candidate.

bullets.title: TSM hits all-time high +7.2%; foundry industry posts record $48.8B in 1Q26
bullets.body: TSM surged 7.2% to an all-time high. Foundry industry revenue hit a record $48.8B in 1Q26 (+32% y/y), with TSMC's market share widening to 95%+. TSMC Arizona Phase 1 net profit in 1Q26 alone exceeded all of CY25. N3 remains the primary AI supply bottleneck.

bullets.title: MSFT rises 2.8% to 4-month high; Wells Fargo bullish on AI push; antitrust risk flagged
bullets.body: Microsoft shares gained 2.8% to an over four-month high. Wells Fargo sees MSFT reaching new highs driven by its homegrown AI push. The company also unveiled Surface Laptop Ultra engineered with NVIDIA and announced new AI models and Windows improvements at Build. Counterpoint: Microsoft flagged as potential next Big Tech antitrust target.

bullets.title: META added: trader views AI CapEx concerns as overblown; adds to position
bullets.body: One fintwit account added to META, calling it 'one of the clearest AI winners, both short- and long-term.' The trader argues the market 'misunderstands the fungibility and ROI mechanics of META's AI spend' and that CapEx concerns are overblown given deeply negative sentiment.

bullets.title: ORCL long-dated call performing strongly; GAI CDS spreads tightening support thesis
bullets.body: An ORCL 1/21/28 c470 call was described as a 'mindbendingly good trade,' driven by both stock appreciation and rising implied volatility. The trader noted sentiment was deeply negative at entry, limiting downside, and flagged tightening Generative AI CDS spreads as supportive of the thesis.

bullets.title: AVGO: JPM Asia supply chain checks flag MediaTek gaining Google TPUv9 share
bullets.body: JPM Asia supply chain checks suggest MediaTek's 'Humufish' (v9 TPU with 4 N2 compute dies + 12 HBM4e stacks) is emerging as Google's primary v9 project, potentially displacing Broadcom—flagged as a material negative for AVGO.

bullets.title: CRDO earnings today with 15.4% implied move
bullets.body: Credo Technology (CRDO) reports earnings today with options markets pricing a 15.4% implied move. The trader noted they 'hope it goes the right direction.'

bullets.title: Goldman warns AI trade shifting to leverage/speculation; market 'concentrated and uncomfortable'
bullets.body: Goldman's 1-Delta desk and top trader both flagged structurally elevated conditions: the AI trade is described as 'no longer about quality—it's about leverage and speculation seeking the next SK Hynix.' Separately, Goldman's top trader warned the market is 'more convinced, concentrated, and levered in AI' with 'uncomfortable' undercurrents.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing beats at 54.0 (4-yr high); Atlanta Fed GDPNow slips to 3.0%
bullets.body: May ISM Manufacturing PMI beat expectations at 54.0 (vs. 53.0 est., 52.7 prior), a 4-year high, with new orders surging to 56.8. However, the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model cut Q2 2026 real GDP estimate to +3.0% from +3.8%, and prices paid remained elevated at 82.1.

bullets.title: Oil spikes to $96 Brent on Iran-Hezbollah escalation; Trump dismisses oil concerns
bullets.body: Brent crude rose to $96/bbl (WTI +5.2%) as Iran threatened to 'completely block' the Strait of Hormuz and halted US diplomatic messages. Trump said 'I don't care' about Iran talks ending and was 'not worried' about oil prices, predicting they would fall 'like a rock.'

bullets.title: Software rally and unprofitable tech: Goldman basket gains 27% in May vs Nasdaq +10%
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs' basket of profitless tech companies gained 27% in May, the widest outperformance vs. Nasdaq 100 (+10%) since November 2020. Non-profitable Russell 2000 stocks are also outperforming profitable peers YTD through 5/29/26, reflecting risk-on momentum.

bullets.title: TSLA Norway registrations +28.7% YoY in May; index methodology changes trigger ~$7.7B forced buying
bullets.body: Tesla new registrations in Norway rose 28.7% YoY in May. Separately, Nasdaq, MSCI, and FTSE methodology changes this year triggered an estimated ~$7.7B in combined forced buying of TSLA (Nasdaq-100 ~$4.1B, MSCI ~$3.6B), with Russell reconstitution seen as a potential opportunity in September.
